# Builder

`QuickSave<T>.Builder` is a builder class for constructing `QuickSave<T>` instances.

```csharp
var save = new QuickSave<T>.Builder()
    /* optional methods */
    .Build();
```

***

## Methods

### Build()

```csharp
public QuickSave<T> Build()
```

Applies the configuration and returns a `QuickSave<T>` instance. The save directory is created automatically at this point if it doesn't exist.

***

### UseEncryption(string encryptionKey)

```csharp
public Builder UseEncryption(string encryptionKey)
```

> Available only when the `USE_ENCRYPT` symbol is defined (requires DataProtector).

Enables encryption on save and decryption on load.

| Parameter       | Type     | Description                            |
| --------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `encryptionKey` | `string` | Key used for encryption and decryption |

```csharp
new QuickSave<PlayerData>.Builder()
    .UseEncryption("your-secret-key")
    .Build();
```

***

### UseVersion(int version)

```csharp
public Builder UseVersion(int version)
```

> Available only when the `USE_ENCRYPT` symbol is defined.

Appends a version number to the save file name. Defaults to `0`.

| Parameter | Type  | Description                              |
| --------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `version` | `int` | Version number appended to the file name |

```csharp
new QuickSave<PlayerData>.Builder()
    .UseEncryption("your-secret-key")
    .UseVersion(2)
    .Build();
// → PlayerData_2.acqs
```



---
url: /quick-save/en/api/methods.md

# QuickSave<T> Methods

Public method reference for `QuickSave<T>`.

> Generic constraint: `where T : class`

***

## SaveData

```csharp
public void SaveData(T data)
```

Serializes `data` with MemoryPack and writes it to a file. If encryption is enabled, the binary is encrypted after serialization.

| Parameter | Type | Description        |
| --------- | ---- | ------------------ |
| `data`    | `T`  | The object to save |

```csharp
save.SaveData(player);
```

***

## SaveDataAsync

```csharp
public Task SaveDataAsync(T data)
```

Async version of `SaveData`. Does not block the main thread.

```csharp
await save.SaveDataAsync(player);
```

***

## LoadData

```csharp
public T LoadData()
```

Reads the save file and returns the deserialized object.

| Return value                  | Condition                             |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `T` instance                  | Successfully loaded                   |
| `null`                        | File does not exist                   |
| Throws `InvalidDataException` | File exists but deserialization fails |

```csharp
try
{
    var data = save.LoadData();
    if (data == null) { /* no file */ }
}
catch (InvalidDataException e)
{
    Debug.LogError(e.Message); // corrupted file
}
```

***

## LoadDataAsync

```csharp
public Task<T> LoadDataAsync()
```

Async version of `LoadData`.

```csharp
var data = await save.LoadDataAsync();
```

***

## HasSaveData

```csharp
public bool HasSaveData()
```

Returns `true` if the save file exists, `false` otherwise. Use this to check for a file before calling `LoadData`.

```csharp
if (save.HasSaveData())
{
    var data = save.LoadData();
}
```

***

## DeleteData

```csharp
public void DeleteData()
```

Deletes the save file. Does nothing if the file doesn't exist.

```csharp
save.DeleteData();
```

# Changelog

## \[1.0.3] `latest` — 2026-05-23

### Added

- **`SaveDataAsync(T data)`** — Async save method using `File.WriteAllBytesAsync`. Prevents blocking the main thread during file I/O.
- **`LoadDataAsync()`** — Async load method. Avoids frame drops on large save files or slow storage (especially mobile).
- **`HasSaveData()`** — Check whether a save file exists before attempting to load. Previously, you had to call `LoadData()` and check for `null`.

### Fixed

- **`Builder.UseVersion()` ignored bug** — When `UseVersion(n)` was called, the version value was silently hardcoded to `0` internally. This caused save files to be created at the wrong path when using encryption with versioning.
- **`SaveData<T>` type parameter shadowing** — A structural bug that allowed serializing a different type than the class-level `T` in `QuickSave<T>`. For example, passing a `string` to a `QuickSave<MyData>` instance compiled without error.
- **`LoadData()` error distinction** — Previously, a missing file and a corrupted file were handled ambiguously. Now a missing file returns `null`, while a deserialization failure throws `InvalidDataException`, making the two cases clearly distinguishable.

### Performance

- **Save directory creation optimized** — Previously, `Directory.Exists` was called on every `SaveData`, `LoadData`, and `DeleteData` call. Now the directory is checked and created exactly once at `Build()` time, and the file path is cached in `_filePath`.

***

## \[1.0.2] — 2026-05-16

### Added

- **`DeleteData()`** — Delete the save file (`.acqs`) at runtime. Does not throw if the file doesn't exist.
- **Editor menu `Achieve > Delete Save`** — Unity Editor utility to batch-delete all `.acqs` files in the `quicksave/` directory. Shows a confirmation dialog with the file count and path before deleting.

***

## \[1.0.0] — 2024-01-01

### Added

- Initial package release
- **`SaveData(T data)`** — Binary serialization using MemoryPack
- **`LoadData()`** — Binary deserialization and load
- Save files stored as `.acqs` under `Application.persistentDataPath/quicksave/`
- **Encryption option** — AES encryption via DataProtector integration (`USE_ENCRYPT` define)
- **Versioning** — Append version numbers to file names with `UseVersion(int)` for multi-version save management
- **Builder pattern** — Fluent instance configuration via `QuickSave<T>.Builder`

# Getting Started

## Prerequisite: install MemoryPack

Quick Save depends on MemoryPack. First, install MemoryPack via [NuGetForUnity](https://github.com/GlitchEnzo/NuGetForUnity).

1. Install NuGetForUnity in your project.
2. Open **NuGet > Manage NuGet Packages** from the Unity menu.
3. Search for `MemoryPack` and install it.

## Installation

### Unity Package Manager (UPM) — recommended

1. Open **Window > Package Manager**.
2. Click the `+` button in the top left → **Add package from git URL...**.
3. Enter the URL below and click **Add**.

```
https://github.com/achieveonepark/QuickSave.git#1.0.3
```

### Editing manifest.json directly

Add to `dependencies` in `Packages/manifest.json`.

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "com.achieve.quick-save": "https://github.com/achieveonepark/QuickSave.git#1.0.3"
  }
}
```


> **Info**
> 
> If you need encryption, also install the [DataProtector](https://github.com/achieveonepark/DataProtector) package. When DataProtector is present, the `USE_ENCRYPT` symbol is defined automatically, enabling the `UseEncryption()` and `UseVersion()` methods. See [Usage › Encryption & Versioning](/quick-save/en/usage/encryption.md) for details.
> 


## Quick start

### 1. Define the data class to save

Add the `[MemoryPackable]` attribute and the `partial` keyword to the class you want to serialize with MemoryPack.

```csharp
using MemoryPack;

[MemoryPackable]
public partial class PlayerData
{
    public string Name;
    public int Level;
    public float HP;
    public long Gold;
}
```

### 2. Create a QuickSave instance

Create an instance with the `Builder` pattern. The save directory (`persistentDataPath/quicksave/`) is prepared at creation time.

```csharp
using Achieve.QuickSave;

var save = new QuickSave<PlayerData>.Builder().Build();
```

### 3. Save, load, delete

```csharp
var player = new PlayerData { Name = "Hero", Level = 1, HP = 100f, Gold = 0 };

save.SaveData(player);                 // save

if (save.HasSaveData())                // check existence
{
    PlayerData loaded = save.LoadData(); // load
    Debug.Log(loaded.Name);            // "Hero"
}

save.DeleteData();                     // delete
```

## Next steps

- [Usage › Basic Usage](/quick-save/en/usage/basic.md)
- [API › QuickSave\<T> Methods](/quick-save/en/api/methods.md)

# Introduction

**A lightweight save system for Unity.**
Save your game data quickly and safely with MemoryPack-based binary serialization.

## Features

- ⚡ **High-performance serialization** — Fast binary serialization/deserialization using Cysharp's MemoryPack.
- 🔒 **Encryption support** — Encrypt saved data to prevent tampering and inspection.
- 🧩 **Concise API** — Compose your save/load flow at a glance with the builder pattern.

## Quick links

- [Getting Started](/quick-save/en/getting-started.md)
- [Usage](/quick-save/en/usage/basic.md)
- [API Reference](/quick-save/en/api/methods.md)
- [GitHub](https://github.com/achieveonepark/quick-save)

# Async Save / Load

## Why Async?

`SaveData` / `LoadData` use `File.WriteAllBytes` / `File.ReadAllBytes` internally. On large save files or slow storage (especially mobile), this can momentarily block the main thread.

`SaveDataAsync` / `LoadDataAsync` use `File.WriteAllBytesAsync` / `File.ReadAllBytesAsync` to avoid blocking the main thread.

***

## SaveDataAsync

```csharp
await save.SaveDataAsync(playerData);
```

***

## LoadDataAsync

```csharp
PlayerData loaded = await save.LoadDataAsync();

if (loaded == null)
{
    // No save file
}
```

***

## Full Example (async/await)

```csharp
using Achieve.QuickSave;
using UnityEngine;

public class SaveManager : MonoBehaviour
{
    private QuickSave<PlayerData> _save;

    void Awake()
    {
        _save = new QuickSave<PlayerData>.Builder().Build();
    }

    public async void OnSaveButtonClicked(PlayerData player)
    {
        await _save.SaveDataAsync(player);
        Debug.Log("Saved");
    }

    public async void OnLoadButtonClicked()
    {
        try
        {
            PlayerData data = await _save.LoadDataAsync();
            if (data == null)
                Debug.Log("No save data");
            else
                Debug.Log($"Loaded: {data.Name}");
        }
        catch (System.IO.InvalidDataException e)
        {
            Debug.LogError($"Save file corrupted: {e.Message}");
        }
    }
}
```

***

## Using with UniTask

If UniTask is in your project, you can convert `Task` to `UniTask`.

```csharp
using Cysharp.Threading.Tasks;

public async UniTaskVoid SaveAsync(PlayerData player)
{
    await _save.SaveDataAsync(player).AsUniTask();
}
```

# Basic Usage

## Preparing a Data Class

Two requirements for the class you want to serialize with MemoryPack:

- `[MemoryPackable]` attribute
- `partial` keyword

```csharp
using MemoryPack;

[MemoryPackable]
public partial class InventoryData
{
    public List<string> Items;
    public int Capacity;
}
```

> The generic constraint on `QuickSave<T>` is `where T : class`. Structs are not supported.

***

## Creating an Instance via Builder

```csharp
var save = new QuickSave<InventoryData>.Builder().Build();
```

When `Build()` is called, the save directory (`persistentDataPath/quicksave/`) is created if it doesn't exist. Subsequent calls to `SaveData` / `LoadData` incur no directory check overhead.

***

## SaveData

```csharp
var inventory = new InventoryData
{
    Items = new List<string> { "Sword", "Shield" },
    Capacity = 20
};

save.SaveData(inventory);
```

The file is saved at `{persistentDataPath}/quicksave/InventoryData.acqs`.

***

## HasSaveData

Check whether the save file exists before loading.

```csharp
if (save.HasSaveData())
{
    // Load only when a file exists
}
```

***

## LoadData

```csharp
InventoryData loaded = save.LoadData();
```

- Returns `null` if the file doesn't exist.
- Throws `InvalidDataException` if the file exists but deserialization fails — allowing you to distinguish between a missing file and a corrupted one.

```csharp
try
{
    var data = save.LoadData();
    if (data == null)
    {
        // No save file → use defaults
    }
}
catch (InvalidDataException e)
{
    Debug.LogError($"Save file corrupted: {e.Message}");
    save.DeleteData(); // Remove corrupted file and restart
}
```

***

## DeleteData

```csharp
save.DeleteData();
```

Does nothing if the file doesn't exist. No exception is thrown.

***

## Deleting Saves in the Editor

Use the Unity Editor menu **Achieve > Delete Save** to delete all `.acqs` files in the `quicksave/` directory. A confirmation dialog is shown before deletion.

# Encryption & Versioning

## Prerequisites

The encryption feature is only active when the [DataProtector](https://github.com/achieveonepark/DataProtector) package is installed.

Once DataProtector is installed, the Assembly Definition automatically defines the `USE_ENCRYPT` symbol, and the Builder's `UseEncryption()` and `UseVersion()` methods become available.

***

## UseEncryption

```csharp
var save = new QuickSave<PlayerData>.Builder()
    .UseEncryption("my-secret-key-32chars")
    .Build();
```

- `SaveData` / `SaveDataAsync`: serializes then encrypts before writing.
- `LoadData` / `LoadDataAsync`: decrypts then deserializes.

> Keep your encryption key safe. Changing the key will make existing save files unreadable.

***

## UseVersion

Specifying a version appends the version number to the file name, letting you separate saves across game updates.

```csharp
var saveV1 = new QuickSave<PlayerData>.Builder()
    .UseEncryption("my-key")
    .UseVersion(1)
    .Build();

var saveV2 = new QuickSave<PlayerData>.Builder()
    .UseEncryption("my-key")
    .UseVersion(2)
    .Build();
```

Resulting file paths:

```
{persistentDataPath}/quicksave/PlayerData_1.acqs   ← v1
{persistentDataPath}/quicksave/PlayerData_2.acqs   ← v2
```

***

## Migration Pattern

Example of migrating from an old version's save file to a new one.

```csharp
var oldSave = new QuickSave<PlayerDataV1>.Builder()
    .UseEncryption("my-key")
    .UseVersion(1)
    .Build();

var newSave = new QuickSave<PlayerData>.Builder()
    .UseEncryption("my-key")
    .UseVersion(2)
    .Build();

if (oldSave.HasSaveData() && !newSave.HasSaveData())
{
    PlayerDataV1 legacy = oldSave.LoadData();
    PlayerData migrated = Migrate(legacy);
    newSave.SaveData(migrated);
    oldSave.DeleteData();
}
```

***

## Encryption Only (No Version)

If `UseVersion` is not called, the version defaults to `0` and the file name becomes `TypeName_0.acqs`.

```csharp
var save = new QuickSave<PlayerData>.Builder()
    .UseEncryption("my-key")
    // UseVersion not called → _0.acqs
    .Build();
```
